questions.question: Why does `re.findall("\bcat\b", text)` (a normal, non-raw string) usually find nothing?
options: findall does not support word boundaries
Python turns \b into a backspace character before re sees the pattern
Word boundaries only work with re.compile
questions.explanation: String escapes are processed first, so "\b" is a backspace (\x08). A raw string r"\b" passes the backslash through so re reads a word boundary.

questions.question: Which function should you use to validate that an entire string is a 6-digit PIN code?
questions.explanation: fullmatch requires the pattern to consume the whole string. match only anchors at the start, so it accepts trailing garbage.

questions.question: What does `re.findall(r"<.+>", "bold")` return?
questions.explanation: Greedy quantifiers match as much as possible, so .+ runs to the last >. The lazy form .+? or the class [^>]+ yields each tag separately.

questions.question: Why might `"café" == "cafe\u0301"` be False even though both look identical?
options: Python compares strings by memory address
One uses a composed é and the other e plus a combining accent; normalising both with unicodedata.normalize("NFC", ...) makes them equal
String literals with accents are bytes, not str
casefold() must be called before any comparison
questions.explanation: Unicode allows different code point sequences for the same visible text. Normalising to NFC (or NFKC for search keys) before comparing removes the difference.
